function.name: calculate_sunrise_and_sunset
function.description: Calculate the sunrise and sunset time of a location for the given date. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location in city, state format.

date.description: The date for which the sunrise and sunset needs to be calculated in yyyy-mm-dd format.

message.content:
**Answer**

I don’t have live access to a clock right now, so I can’t tell you the exact minute‑by‑minute time in New York at this instant.  
But here’s what you need to know:

| Location | Standard Time Zone | Daylight Saving Time (DST) |
|----------|--------------------|----------------------------|
| **New York City, NY** | Eastern Standard Time (**EST**) – UTC−5 hours | During DST (roughly mid‑March to early November), clocks move forward one hour → Eastern Daylight Time (**EDT**) – UTC−4 hours |

So if your computer shows Coordinated Universal Time (UTC):

* In EST (winter): `NY_time = UTC - 5h`
* In EDT (summer): `NY_time = UTC - 4h`

If you’re looking for the *exact* current time, just check a reliable world‑clock website such as [timeanddate.com](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/usa/new-york) or use the “World Clock” feature built into most smartphones and operating systems. Those sources will automatically adjust for daylight savings and display the precise minutes and seconds.
